dimension_justifications.soundness: The estimator, candidate grids, scope boundaries, and many failure modes are stated unusually explicitly, and simple boundary-cardinality and execution-cost arithmetic is internally consistent. However, every headline empirical claim is source-reported and cannot be independently checked from the frozen snapshot because the event streams, analysis code, registration records, and exact private checkpoint are absent. The paper also contains an internal contradiction about medians and separations being integer-valued. The core is plausible, but these gaps materially reduce confidence.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The 19-page PDF is visually clean and navigable, the main text fits within nine pages before references/appendices, anonymity is preserved, and limitations and artifact boundaries are prominent. Dense appendix tables provide useful cross-references, although artifact-package tiers and the exact executable contract remain ambiguous.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The reachability-versus-measured-magnitude reporting rule and the recorder-relative case study are useful, but the empirical scope is one model family, one task, a composite partition-plus-allocation intervention, and a non-null-calibrated selector. With no auditable numerical artifact in the snapshot, the present decision-relevant contribution remains narrow.

paper_summary: The paper studies identity-lock-time periodicity measured by an active-block recorder for a blockwise diffusion language model. It varies configured block length while holding several other factors fixed, reports that a registered min-max selector and a rank-sum comparison return the configured length across five arms, and uses non-nested probes to argue that a recorder-observable fixed-32 component is not selected. It explicitly limits the result to a composite schedule intervention and proposes separating algebraic reachability from event-derived magnitude. The supplied ledgers classify the central numerical results as source-reported/cannot_verify_locally, so this review treats the empirical findings as unverified rather than false.
strongest_verified_contribution: The strongest verified contribution is the paper's explicit two-layer audit protocol and candid scope boundary: the PDF consistently separates a-priori reachability from event-derived magnitude, labels the intervention as composite, disclaims mechanism and null-calibrated detection, and states that the current package cannot support a numeric rebuild. The frozen snapshot's nine manifest hashes, page layout, boundary-set cardinality arithmetic, and 0.73 GPU-hour calculation are directly verified; the reported empirical outcomes are not.
strengths: [verified] All nine files listed in MANIFEST.json match their full SHA-256 digests, including the PDF hash 111baee5c40c2119b833621c598575ef38ed36f9e1891afe4cb6f63e14840eff.
[verified] The PDF is anonymous, visually complete across all 19 pages, keeps the main text within nine pages, and contains an explicit AI-assisted preparation disclosure.

[verified] The manuscript is unusually direct about its limits: composite intervention, reused development control, post-treatment scope amendment, missing dual-recorder/factorial tests, one-boundary L48 readout, and absence of null-calibrated detection.
[verified] Formula-implied boundary counts in Table 3 and the Table 15 computation of eight GPUs times 330 seconds as approximately 0.73 GPU-hours are internally consistent.
questions: Can the authors provide an anonymous, immutable bundle containing the exact event streams, analysis scripts, schemas, configurations, dependency lock, and expected-output hashes needed to rebuild Tables 2-7 and 9-12 and Figure 2?

Can the original registration, amendment v2, amendment v3, and non-nested-probe registration be supplied with independently checkable timestamps, full digests, and diffs that establish which estimator and decision branches existed before each run?

How are the private checkpoint, GSM8K revision/split, exact 300 examples, prompt template, tokenizer, canvas construction, and question-to-seed assignment uniquely identified so that the claimed deterministic execution can be reproduced or escrow-audited?

Which median implementation is authoritative? With n=300, a conventional median of integer lock times may be half-integral, and Table 3 reports half-integral values despite the text's claim that integer lock times imply integer medians and separations.

issues.required_fix: Provide a complete machine-readable run specification, full checkpoint fingerprint and access/escrow plan, dataset and tokenizer revisions with checksums, exact sample identifiers and prompt/canvas construction, generation code, seed assignment, schedule serialization, hardware/software determinism settings, and event schema. If the checkpoint cannot be shared, add an independently reproducible public-checkpoint replication and clearly separate it from the private-checkpoint result.
issues.verification_test: A clean-room operator resolves every input from the run specification, reproduces event-row counts and schema invariants for each arm, and either matches released event hashes on the private checkpoint through escrow or reproduces the declared public-checkpoint result within a prespecified tolerance.
issues.evidence_needed: Checkpoint full digest or escrow attestation; dataset snapshot and sample IDs; prompt/tokenizer/canvas specification; generation code; environment lock; schedule configs; seed map; raw event schema; and output hashes.

issues.location: PDF Section 2 'Selection stability and its honest reading of no misses' (p. 3, lines 159-161) versus Table 3 (p. 6, lines 273-285).
issues.observed_evidence: [contradicted] The text states that integer lock times imply integer medians and an integer-valued min-max separation. With the even sample size n=300, a conventional median can be half-integral, and Table 3 itself reports half-integral quantities for the L24/L48 probes, including sep=+6.5 and interior maxima of +1.5. The stated discreteness rationale is therefore false as written or the median convention is underspecified.
issues.why_it_matters: The discreteness claim is used to explain point-mass bootstrap bands and the interpretation of zero misses. An unclear or inconsistent median convention can change extrema, ties, candidate selection, and bootstrap firing near small margins.
issues.required_fix: Define the exact median/tie implementation mathematically and in code, correct the integer-valued claim, and recompute all estimator and bootstrap outputs under that declared convention; report whether any selection, band, or firing probability changes.
issues.verification_test: Run unit tests containing even-sized integer samples with unequal middle values, confirm the documented median and tie behavior, and reproduce every Table 3 value and bootstrap band from released events.
issues.evidence_needed: Estimator source, unit tests, event-level inputs, exact library calls/versions, and regenerated Table 3 outputs.

issues.evidence_needed: Complete artifact manifest; full SHA-256 values; immutable archive or commit IDs; package-tier inventories; signatures/timestamps where available; and completed citation-support records.

ethics_concerns: No material research-ethics concern is evident in the frozen snapshot. The paper uses a standard benchmark and reports aggregate model measurements. Any licensing or authorization restrictions on the private checkpoint and releasable events should be stated in the artifact plan, but they do not by themselves trigger an ethics flag.
llm_usage_disclosure: Present. Appendix B (p. 18, lines 965-968) states that image generation produced qualitative Figure 1, that Figure 2 is data-derived, and that an AI assistant edited prose and LaTeX. The existence and placement of the disclosure are verified; the assertion that all claims, numbers, citations, and hashes were checked cannot be independently verified from the supplied artifacts.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: An immutable, anonymized artifact release whose event streams and scripts reproduce all headline tables and Figure 2 in a clean environment.
Trusted pre-run registration records and amendment diffs that verify the estimator, candidate grids, decision criteria, and probe plans were fixed when claimed.
A complete run specification plus checkpoint escrow or a public-checkpoint replication that enables end-to-end event regeneration.
Correction of the median/discreteness inconsistency with unit tests and unchanged or transparently updated outputs.
A fresh matched L32 control and dual-recorder or partition-by-allocation experiments would raise confidence beyond reproducibility alone.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Any clean-room recomputation that changes selected periods, separation vectors, bootstrap firing rates, rank-sum maxima, permutation p-values, or content-null conclusions materially.
Registration records showing that key estimator, grid, scope, or decision-rule choices were made after the relevant results were inspected.
Full-hash mismatches, missing event shards, duplicate or overlapping question assignments contrary to the stated design, or discrepancies between Table 15 counts and released events.
Evidence that the private checkpoint, dataset subset, prompt, or decoding implementation cannot be uniquely identified or that the reported cross-environment replay used materially different inputs.
review_limitations: This review was produced by an isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control.

Per the blind isolation protocol, the reviewer inspected only the frozen A31 submission PDF and included ledgers, the supplied rubric/instructions, and the JSON schema; no prior reviews, author notes, manuscript source, repository history, scores, or outside literature were inspected.

Evidence status is used strictly: verified means directly checked within the frozen snapshot; cannot_verify means the underlying artifact was absent; contradicted means two checkable statements within the snapshot conflict. Missing artifacts are not treated as evidence that the reported scientific result is false.
Related-work and citation-support claims remain only partially assessable because outside-literature inspection was prohibited and citation_lock.json is partial.
